page: Microsoft Azure F16ads_v7 is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Fadsv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. The configuration includes 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating with a single thread per core under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and it supports Premium Storage. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores all placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores falling in the middle 50% average tier, though Geekbench multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reach the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached operations register in the average range, while Passmark memory scores are in the top 25%. In LLM inference, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds for small 135M models, but drops to average performance for medium 7B and large 70B models.

The F16ads_v7 offers a balanced resource density with its 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and integrated high-capacity NVMe storage. This hardware profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring fast single-thread execution and local storage speed without the overhead of a GPU. Tradeoffs include average multi-core scaling and moderate memory bandwidth under heavy parallel loads. The instance is suited for text and image processing, web serving, database operations, and lightweight language model inference.
